name: module-edit-autosave
description: 0.0.8 plan 2, M-1 to M-4 (the hello project, with files.autoSave afterDelay): a module interface is written function by function while its importer is open. Each pause with half a statement on the screen (the runner leaves the broken text up for 0.5 to 2.5 s) is written to disk once a second has passed since the last key, so clangd fails to build the module, over and over. 0.0.7 took that for a broken module: it dooms the module's own file and its importers (RP1.1), takes them from clangd, publishes one 'module-failed' diagnostic without a position for each, and answers their completions from mcppls's own engine (empty, in 2 ms) until the next save hands them back, so the files flip every few seconds and, in the reproduction, 106 of 223 completions in the module being edited were empty. A module being edited is not a broken module: nothing is doomed (M-1), clangd keeps answering in the module and in the importer, a completion clangd cannot be asked about still offers the file's words and keywords (M-2), a preparation that waits for an edit is not stalled (M-3), and no 'module-failed' diagnostic is published. The importer holds a probe line, `int probe_value = 1; probe_v`, inside main(); a correct answer has `probe_value`, and none may be empty. One typing check on the module interface, 30 s at 10 Hz, autosave 1000 ms after the last key (autosave-idle-ms); the budgets are 0 for everything that is a defect and 2 s for the completions of both files, which clangd answers in tens of milliseconds on a project this size.
